title.en: Deal with US not imminent, Iran says
title.zh: 鲁比奥称“稳固”的伊朗协议可能周一达成

summary.en: US media reports indicate that a potential deal for a 60-day ceasefire extension in the region is under discussion, which would also involve the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz.
summary.zh: 美国媒体报道称，一项可能达成的协议正在讨论中，该协议将包括延长60天停火，并重新开放霍尔木兹海峡。

body.en:
Iran says some progress has been reached in talks with the US, but a deal "is not imminent".

Foreign ministry spokesman Esmail Baqai's remarks came after US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said an agreement could possibly be reached on Monday.

"It is correct to say that we have reached a conclusion on a large portion of the issues under discussion," Baqai said in Tehran on Monday. "But to say that this means the signing of an agreement is imminent - no-one can make such a claim."

The memorandum of understanding reportedly involves a 60-day ceasefire extension, reopening the Strait of Hormuz and a plan for further negotiations over Iran's nuclear programme.

At the weekend, President Donald Trump suggested the sides were closing a deal, even though he later said he had instructed negotiators "not to rush into" one.

On Monday, Rubio told reporters in the Indian capital, Delhi: "We thought we might have some news last night. Maybe today."

Cautioning "I wouldn't read too much into it", Rubio said: "It takes a little while to hear back from Iran."

CBS News, the BBC's US partner, has reported that US intelligence believes Iran's Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei - who was injured in an Israeli strike on the first day of the war which killed his father and predecessor - is holed up in an undisclosed location, making communication with his envoys difficult and therefore delaying pace of talks with the US.

According to US media, the mooted deal is not a final settlement - instead it leaves some of the thorniest issues to be negotiated later, including the scope and timing of Iranian sanctions relief, the release of frozen Iranian funds, and Washington's demands for Iran to curb its nuclear ambitions.

"So we have, what I think is a pretty solid thing on the table in terms of their ability to open up the Straits," he said referring to the Strait of Hormuz - the crucial waterway where 20% of the world's oil and liquefied natural gas passes and which Iran has been blocking.

Oil prices fell sharply and Asian stock markets rose on Monday on hopes of an agreement.

The reported deal has split Trump's Republicans, with some publicly arguing it is too lenient on Iran.

Senator Ted Cruz said it would be "a disastrous mistake", while Roger Wicker, who chairs the Senate Armed Services Committee, said a 60-day ceasefire would mean "everything accomplished by Operation Epic Fury would be for naught!"

Senator Lindsey Graham, who is a close Trump ally, also criticised any deal that would leave Iran perceived as being a dominant force in the region.

Trump responded by dismissing his critics as "losers" and saying "the deal with Iran will either be a great and meaningful one, or there will be no deal".

Even in a best case scenario, the effects of a deal are unlikely...
body.zh: 美国国务卿马可·卢比奥表示，美国和伊朗谈判代表“摆在桌面上的事情非常可靠”，两国可能会在周一达成一项结束战争的协议。 在他发表此番言论之前，唐纳德·特朗普总统表示，他已指示谈判代表“不要急于达成协议”，此前他曾暗示已经接近达成协议。 据报道，协议涉及延长停火60天、重新开放霍尔木兹海峡以及就伊朗核计划进行进一步谈判的计划。 由于达成协议的希望，油价大幅下跌，亚洲股市周一上涨。 “我们的工作仍在进行中。正如我所说，你知道，我们认为昨晚可能会得到一些消息。也许今天，”卢比奥周一在印度首都德里表示。 “所以，我认为就他们开放海峡的能力而言，我们已经摆在桌面上，”他指的是霍尔木兹海峡。世界上20%的石油和液化天然气都经过这条重要的水道，而伊朗一直在封锁这条海峡。 卢比奥警告称“我不会对此进行太多解读”，并表示“需要一段时间才能收到伊朗的回复”。 英国广播公司(BBC)的美国合作伙伴哥伦比亚广播公司新闻报道称，美国情报部门认为，伊朗最高领导人——在战争第一天在以色列的袭击中受伤——躲藏在一个秘密地点，这使得与其特使的沟通变得困难，从而推迟了与美国的谈判进度。 伊朗外交部发言人埃斯梅尔·巴格哈伊(Esmail Baghaei)周末表示，双方距离达成协议“非常接近但又非常遥远”。 美国媒体称，拟议中的协议并不是最终解决方案，而是将一些最棘手的问题留待以后进行谈判，包括伊朗制裁解除的范围和时间、释放冻结的伊朗资金以及华盛顿要求伊朗遏制其核野心。 报道称，特朗普的共和党人对此产生了分歧，一些人公开认为该协议对伊朗过于宽容。 参议员泰德·克鲁兹表示，这将是“一个灾难性的错误”，而参议院军事委员会主席罗杰·威克则表示，60 天的停火将意味着“史诗愤怒行动所取得的一切都将化为乌有！” 特朗普的亲密盟友、参议员林赛·格雷厄姆也批评任何会让伊朗被视为该地区主导力量的协议。 特朗普回应称，他没有“听取失败者的意见，他们对自己一无所知的事情持批评态度”。 “如果我与伊朗达成协议，这将是一项良好且适当的协议，”他在《真相社会》上写道。 2月28日，美国和以色列对伊朗发动大范围打击，引发中东冲突。伊朗的回应是攻击以色列和美国在海湾的盟国，并有效关闭了海峡...

reflection.en: Even temporary ceasefires and diplomatic efforts, like the one being discussed, are vital steps towards alleviating suffering and creating space for dialogue. Such initiatives remind us of the call to be peacemakers in a world often marked by conflict.
reflection.zh: 即使是暂时的停火和外交努力，如正在讨论的这项协议，也是缓解苦难和为对话创造空间的至关重要的一步。这样的举措提醒我们，在一个常常充满冲突的世界中，要努力成为缔造和平的人。

verse.textEn: Blessed are the peacemakers, for they will be called children of God.
verse.textZh: 使人和睦的人有福了，因为他们必称为神的儿子。

title.en: Currently no active leak from failing chemical tank, California officials say
title.zh: 加州官员称，故障化学品储罐目前没有活跃泄漏

summary.en: California officials have stated there is currently no active leak from a failing chemical tank that contains a highly volatile and flammable substance. The tank had been at risk of a major spillage or explosion.
summary.zh: 加州官员表示，一个装有高度易燃易爆物质的故障化学品储罐目前没有活跃泄漏。该储罐此前一直面临着大规模泄漏或爆炸的风险。

body.en:
California fire officials say there is "currently no active leak" from a failing chemical tank in Orange County.

The tank, which contains thousands of gallons of methyl methacrylate - a highly volatile and flammable substance used to make plastic - has been at risk of either a major spillage or an explosion. Crews have worked through the night from Sunday into Monday to assess the risk.

Tens of thousands of people are under evacuation orders as a precaution, and a state of emergency has been declared by Gavin Newsom, the state governor.

Officials are hopeful the pressure that has built up inside the tank is being gradually released by a crack that has formed - potentially avoiding a disaster.

"Continuous live atmospheric monitoring confirms there are no chemicals leaking," the Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) officials wrote in a social media post on Sunday evening. They also denied any suggestion the tank had suffered more than one crack.

The cause of the incident is under investigation, and emergency crews have sprayed the tank with water to try to stabilise its temperature following some rapid heat increases since Thursday.

Explaining the purpose of Sunday's "all-night mission", the county's interim fire chief, TJ McGovern, said crews wanted to confirm the pressure in the tank had been released.

The hope was to ensure the "Bleve [Boiling Liquid Expanding Vapor Explosion] threat is eliminated", said McGovern. "The Bleve threat is the worst-case catastrophic event that we've been talking about. We are not there yet."

The aerospace facility is in the city of Garden Grove, about 35 miles (56km) south-east of Los Angeles. It is operated by GKN Aerospace, which has apologised to local residents.

At an earlier stage, officials expressed hope that emergency teams could relieve the pressure issue by slowing the rate of the chemical reactions that were causing the substances to heat up inside the tank.

"Letting this thing just fail and blow up is unacceptable to us," said Craig Covey, Orange County Fire Authority division chief.

Officials had also been developing "very aggressive plans" for a scenario in which the tank's integrity fails, Covey added. They have been creating dykes and dams to contain any chemicals if the tank does spill - with the aim of preventing any substances from reaching storm drains or the ocean.

The cities of Garden Grove, Stanton, Anaheim, Cypress, Westminster, and Buena Park are all affected by the evacuation orders.

A number of schools have closed as a precaution, and the exits of several major roads have been shut to limit access to the area.

However, the nearby Disneyland theme park is outside the evacuation zone and has been operating as normal.

body.zh: 加州消防官员表示，奥兰治县一个发生故障的化学品罐“目前没有发生主动泄漏”。 该罐内装有数千加仑甲基丙烯酸甲酯（一种用于制造塑料的高度挥发性易燃物质），存在严重泄漏或爆炸的风险。工作人员从周日到周一通宵工作来评估风险。 作为预防措施，数万人已收到疏散令，该州州长加文·纽瑟姆已宣布进入紧急状态。 官员们希望储罐内积聚的压力能够通过形成的裂缝逐渐释放，从而可能避免灾难。 橙县消防局（OCFA）官员周日晚上在社交媒体帖子中写道：“持续的实时大气监测证实没有化学物质泄漏。”他们还否认任何有关坦克遭受不止一处裂缝的说法。 事故原因正在调查中，自周四以来气温急剧上升，应急人员向水箱喷水，试图稳定水箱温度。 该县临时消防队长 TJ 麦戈文在解释周日“通宵任务”的目的时表示，工作人员希望确认水箱内的压力已释放。 麦戈文表示，希望确保“消除 Bleve（沸腾液体膨胀蒸气爆炸）威胁”。 “布莱夫威胁是我们一直在谈论的最坏情况的灾难性事件。我们还没有到那一步。” 该航空航天设施位于洛杉矶东南约 35 英里（56 公里）处的加登格罗夫市。该飞机由吉凯恩航空航天公司运营，该公司已向当地居民道歉。 早些时候，官员们表示希望应急小组能够通过减缓导致储罐内物质升温的化学反应速度来缓解压力问题。 奥兰治县消防局部门负责人克雷格·科维说：“让这件事失败并爆炸对我们来说是不可接受的。” 科维补充说，官员们还一直在制定“非常积极的计划”，以应对坦克完整性失效的情况。他们一直在建造堤坝和水坝，以在储罐泄漏时容纳任何化学物质，目的是防止任何物质进入雨水渠或海洋。 加登格罗夫、斯坦顿、阿纳海姆、赛普拉斯、威斯敏斯特和布埃纳帕克等城市都受到疏散令的影响。 作为预防措施，许多学校已经关闭，几条主要道路的出口也已关闭，以限制进入该地区。 不过，附近的迪士尼主题公园位于疏散区之外，一直正常运营。 周五，当地居民马克在接受当地媒体 NBC LA 采访时...

reflection.en: News of a dangerous chemical tank being monitored, with no active leak, reminds us of the wisdom in foreseeing potential hazards. It highlights the importance of vigilance and proactive measures to prevent harm, allowing communities to take refuge from looming threats.
reflection.zh: 有关危险化学品储罐受到监控且目前没有活跃泄漏的消息，提醒我们预见潜在危险的智慧。这突显了警惕性和积极预防措施的重要性，使社区能够免受迫在眉睫的威胁。

verse.textEn: The prudent see danger and take refuge, but the simple keep going and pay the penalty.
verse.textZh: 通达人见祸藏躲；愚蒙人前往受害。

title.en: Clashes as Venezuelan prisoners protest over alleged mistreatment
title.zh: 委内瑞拉囚犯因涉嫌虐待而发生冲突

summary.en: The prisoners insisted their protest was peaceful but that security forces deployed to quell it opened fire.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及公义、尊严与问责。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Violent clashes have erupted between inmates and security personnel at a prison in the Venezuelan state of Barinas.

Extra security forces were deployed to the jail after prisoners climbed the roof and burned mattresses in protest at their alleged mistreatment.

Organisations lobbying for prisoners' rights have long denounced the poor conditions at many of Venezuela's penitentiaries.

Non-governmental organisation Venezuelan Prison Observatory (OVP) said that the inmates at the jail, known as Injuba, had been complaining for more than a week about their treatment under the prison's new director.

They allege they were violently searched, kept in solitary confinement and mistreated.

The prison director has so far not publicly commented, nor has the government of interim President Delcy Rodríguez.

In footage published by OVP, groups of inmates can be seen protesting on the roof, with some burning mattresses.

In one video, a man can be seen showing wounds on his torso and his arm, with another man shouting "they're shooting at us".

In another recording shared by OVP, a woman wearing dark glasses and a face mask addresses Rodríguez directly and demands that the minister of prisons and Injuba's director resign.

She insists that their protest is peaceful before stating their demands, which include medicine for prisoners who have tuberculosis.

OVP has long drawn attention to the poor conditions in Venezuelan jails, with the organisation warning that many do not meet the "minimum standards" which should be guaranteed by law.

Since the United States seized Venezuelan leader Nicolás Maduro in a military operation in the capital, Caracas, on 3 January, US pressure has led to the release of hundreds of political prisoners.

However, more than 400 are still behind bars, according to pressure group Foro Penal.

While Injuba is not one of the prisons where most political prisoners are usually kept, Venezuela's Committee for the Freedom of Political Prisoners expressed its solidarity with the inmates there, alleging that "punishment, hunger, solitary confinement, torture and inhumane conditions" were being used to control and subdue prisoners and "formed part of prison policy".

In March, the United Nations' High Commissioner for Human Rights, Volker Türk, said that his office had been receiving reports alleging that detainees had continued to be tortured in Venezuela following Maduro's ouster by the US.
body.zh: 委内瑞拉巴里纳斯州一所监狱的囚犯和保安人员之间爆发暴力冲突。 在囚犯爬上屋顶并焚烧床垫以抗议他们所遭受的虐待后，额外的安全部队被部署到监狱。 游说囚犯权利的组织长期以来一直谴责委内瑞拉许多监狱条件恶劣。 非政府组织委内瑞拉监狱观察站（OVP）表示，这所名为“Injuba”的监狱的囚犯一周多来一直在抱怨新监狱长领导下的待遇。 他们声称自己遭到暴力搜查、单独监禁和虐待。 到目前为止，监狱长尚未公开发表评论，临时总统德尔西·罗德里格斯政府也没有公开发表评论。 在 OVP 发布的视频中，可以看到一群囚犯在屋顶上抗议，一些床垫正在燃烧。 在一段视频中，可以看到一名男子的躯干和手臂上有伤口，另一名男子大喊“他们在向我们开枪”。 在 OVP 分享的另一段录音中，一名戴着墨镜和口罩的妇女直接向罗德里格斯讲话，要求监狱部长和因朱巴主任辞职。 她坚称他们的抗议是和平的，然后才提出他们的要求，其中包括为患有肺结核的囚犯提供药品。 OVP 长期以来一直引起人们对委内瑞拉监狱条件恶劣的关注，该组织警告说，许多监狱不符合法律应保障的“最低标准”。 自1月3日美国在首都加拉加斯的军事行动中抓获委内瑞拉领导人尼古拉斯·马杜罗以来，在美国的压力下，数百名政治犯被释放。 然而，据压力组织 Foro Penal 称，仍有 400 多人仍在监狱中。 虽然因朱巴不是通常关押大多数政治犯的监狱之一，但委内瑞拉政治犯自由委员会表示声援那里的囚犯，声称“惩罚、饥饿、单独监禁、酷刑和不人道条件”被用来控制和制服囚犯，并“构成监狱政策的一部分”。 今年三月，联合国人权事务高级专员沃尔克·蒂尔克表示，他的办公室收到了报告，称马杜罗被美国赶下台后，委内瑞拉的被拘留者继续遭受酷刑。

reflection.en: This story draws attention to justice, dignity, and accountability. Micah 6:8 reminds us to meet sharp headlines with justice tempered by mercy, asking how faithful people can respond with wisdom instead of noise.
reflection.zh: 这则新闻让人想到公义、尊严与问责。Micah 6:8提醒我们，在快速变化的新闻里，仍要以带着怜悯的公义来回应，并学习用祷告与分辨代替情绪化判断。

verse.textEn: What does Yahweh require of you? To act justly and to love mercy and to walk humbly with your God.
verse.textZh: 雅伟向你所要的是什么呢？只要你行公义，好怜悯，存谦卑的心，与你的神同行。

title.en: Senegal's leadership row mounts as parliament speaker resigns
title.zh: 塞内加尔领导层纷争加剧，议会议长辞职

summary.en: El Malick Ndiaye, the speaker of Senegal's parliament, has resigned amidst speculation that his departure is intended to allow the return of ousted Prime Minister Ousmane Sonko to a leadership position.
summary.zh: 塞内加尔议会议长埃尔·马利克·恩迪亚耶辞职，外界猜测此举是为了让被罢免的总理乌斯曼·松科能够重返领导岗位。

body.en:
The Speaker of Senegal's parliament El Malick Ndiaye has resigned from his post days after the country's President Bassirou Diomaye Faye sacked his mentor-turned-deputy, Prime Minister Ousmane Sonko, and dissolved the government .

Some now speculate there are plans to offer the vacant speaker post to Sonko by loyalists in defiance of the president.

In a statement announcing his decision to resign as speaker on Sunday, Ndiaye said it came after "deep reflection" on "the sense of statehood".

"In public responsibilities as well as in the trials of national life, there are times when the interest of the country commands to prioritise integrity, discernment and sense of duty," he added.

MPs have now been asked to meet on Tuesday for a session aimed at bringing Sonko back into parliament and voting for a new speaker.

The former prime minister, who is also the firebrand leader of the Pastef party, was at the top of its list in 2024's legislative elections. Although he was elected, he renounced his legislative duties to continue serving as prime minister.

"I am staying at the prime minister's office. I submitted my resignation letter as a member of parliament," Sonko was quoted as saying two years ago.

However, following the end of his tenure in government, he looks set to return to parliament where his supporters expect him to run for the post of speaker.

With the departure of Sonko and his possible rise to the summit of legislative power, analysts say Faye's power could be significantly limited without parliamentary support.

Sonko's Pastef party already enjoys an absolute majority there - a factor which many say could complicate Faye's ability to introduce policies or reforms.

The country now awaits the appointment of a new prime minister, but uncertainty remains over whether their approval process in parliament would be smooth. Lawmakers have up to three months to approve the nominated candidate.

Meanwhile, the president cannot dissolve parliament until at least two years after the last election. That means any move to prematurely end the mandates of lawmakers before November this year would be considered invalid.

The rift between Faye and Sonko further raises uncertainty over the political future of the debt-crippled West African nation, which is no stranger to leadership tussles.

The 51-year-old ex-prime minister commands massive support across the country, especially among young people. While previously serving as a legislator in the opposition, he was renowned for fiercely challenging former President Macky Sall's policies - a trait which he also demonstrated against his boss Faye.

Sonko would almost certainly have taken the top job had he not been barred from running in 2024's presidential election due to a defamation conviction.

body.en:
At least 19 people have been taken to hospital after a strong smell was reported at a shopping complex in Tokyo, according to media reports.

A police spokesperson said a man had sprayed a substance at a cash machine on the ground floor of the building in the luxury Ginza 6 shopping centre on Monday.

The substance is believed to have been an irritant spray, identified by authorities as likely containing capsaicin - which is found in chilli peppers.

People near the scene reported feeling their throat become painful and itchy, with one 70-year-old woman telling AFP that it started "stinging and hurting" as she approached the ATM.

"By the time I arrived, the commotion had already started, and I thought there might have been a small fire or something," she said.

A large emergency response was present at the scene, including police officers, firefighters and ambulance workers.

Officials dressed in hazmat suits were seen bringing people out of the shopping centre.

Photographs of the scene show cordons in place, with emergency workers hanging sheets of tarp around part of the mall.

title.en: Why are Europe's biggest defense projects in trouble?
title.zh: 欧洲最大的国防项目为何陷入困境？

summary.en: Disputes over leadership, military priorities and industrial control are threatening to fracture Europe's €100 billion fighter jet project — with tensions now spilling into a Franco-German tank project as well.
summary.zh: 围绕领导权、军事优先事项和工业控制权的争议，正威胁着欧洲耗资1000亿欧元的战斗机项目，紧张局势也蔓延到了法德坦克项目。

body.en:
Disputes over leadership, military priorities and industrial control are threatening to fracture Europe's €100 billion fighter jet project — with tensions now spilling into a Franco-German tank project as well.

Europe wanted to build a joint next-generation fighter jet. Instead, the bloc's  biggest defense project may now produce two separate warplanes.

Airbus , which represents the German and Spanish side of the Future Combat Air System (FCAS), told DW it is open to restructuring the program after years of political and industrial disputes. 

That could include a "two-fighter solution" allowing France and Germany to develop separate combat aircraft while still cooperating on drones, sensors and the digital systems linking the battlefield in real time.

The twist: the fighter jet itself may no longer be the project's most important part.

The proposal marks a serious shift for a project once billed as a symbol of Franco-German military unity .

"On FCAS, work is ongoing with the French, German and Spanish governments to decide on the project's way forward," an Airbus spokesperson told DW.

Airbus Chief Executive Guillaume Faury said the wider program still makes sense, even if the fighter jet at its center remains blocked.

"The deadlock of a single pillar should not jeopardize the entire future of this high-tech European capability," he said, adding that Airbus would support a two-fighter option if governments asked for it. 

The dispute is now raising a wider question: Can Europe's biggest powers still build major weapons systems together?

FCAS was launched by France and Germany in 2017, with Spain joining later. Valued at roughly €100 billion ($116 bn), the project aims to deliver a sixth-generation air combat system by around 2040.

The program goes far beyond a next-generation fighter jet. It also includes drones, remote carriers, engines and a "combat cloud" designed to connect aircraft, sensors and battlefield data in real time.

France wants the future aircraft to operate from aircraft carriers and carry nuclear weapons. Being a non-nuclear power itself, Germany does not share those requirements. Berlin has already decided to buy US-made F-35 fighter jets for NATO nuclear-sharing missions.

German Chancellor Friedrich Merz recently acknowledged the divide publicly. He said France needed a nuclear-capable next-generation aircraft, while Germany did not currently require the same capability for the Bundeswehr . If the two sides could not resolve those differences, he warned, "then we can't maintain the project."

title.en: White House shooting suspect identified as update given on injured bystander
title.zh: 白宫枪击案嫌疑人身份确认，受伤旁观者情况更新

summary.en: Court records reveal the suspect Nasire Best had tried to enter White House grounds at a different checkpoint last year.
summary.zh: 法院记录显示，嫌疑人纳西尔·贝斯特去年曾试图从另一个检查站进入白宫。

body.en:
A bystander who was struck by gunfire after a man fired on a checkpoint outside the White House remains in serious but stable condition.

The US Secret Service said the bystander, who has not been identified, suffered a gunshot wound described as not life-threatening. It was not clear how he was shot.

Authorities have released few additional details about the early Saturday evening, local time, shooting. The District of Columbia Metropolitan Police Department said the suspect, identified as 21-year-old Nasire Best, started shooting toward a White House security checkpoint when Secret Service officers returned fire.

It was the third shooting near the president in the past month, after a man stormed the White House Correspondents' Association Dinner in April armed with guns and knives, and Secret Service officers shot and wounded a man who fired at them earlier this month near the Washington Monument.

In a Truth Social post, Trump said the suspect in Saturday's shooting had a "possible obsession with our Country’s most cherished structure".

He also used the shooting to promote the ballroom he is seeking to build on the site of the White House’s former East Wing, saying the shooting "goes to show how important it is, for all future Presidents, to get, what will be, the most safe and secure space of its kind ever built in Washington, D.C".

Trump is asking Congress for US$1 billion ($1.4 billion) for security additions for the White House campus, including the ballroom.

Best had a previous run-in with law enforcement near the White House, according to District of Columbia court records. He was arrested last July for trying to enter White House grounds near a different checkpoint. He failed to heed officers' commands to stop, claimed to be Jesus Christ and said he wanted to be arrested.

Best was a track and field athlete at Dundalk High School in Baltimore, from which he graduated in 2023.

A woman who identified herself as Best’s mother told The Washington Post that she learned about the shooting on social media and was in disbelief.

title.en: Trump tells US negotiators 'not to rush' into peace deal with Iran
title.zh: 特朗普告诉美国谈判代表“不要急于”与伊朗达成和平协议

summary.en: The US president has instructed negotiators not to hasten a peace agreement with Iran, tempering expectations for a permanent ceasefire, despite earlier indications that a deal was largely complete.

body.en:
United States President Donald Trump said the US will not rush into any deal with Iran, as his administration played down hopes of an imminent breakthrough in the three-month-old war that had been raised a day earlier.

The US blockade on Iranian ships in the Strait of Hormuz would "remain in full force and effect until an agreement is reached, certified, and signed", Trump wrote on Truth Social on Monday morning.

"The negotiations are proceeding in an orderly and constructive manner, and I have informed my representatives not to rush into a deal," he said.

There was no immediate response from Iran's government. But Tasnim news agency, which is linked to Iran's Revolutionary Guards, said the US was still obstructing parts of a potential deal, including Iran's demand for the release of frozen funds.

A day earlier, Trump said the US and Iran had "largely negotiated" a memorandum of understanding on a peace deal that would reopen the Strait of Hormuz, which before the conflict carried one-fifth of global oil and liquefied natural gas shipments.

Trump, whose approval ratings have been hit by the war's impact on US energy prices, has repeatedly played up the prospect of an agreement to end the conflict that the US and Israel started on 28 February. A tenuous ceasefire has been in place since early April.

The two sides remain at odds on several difficult issues, such as Iran's nuclear ambitions, Israel's war in Lebanon with the Iranian-backed Hezbollah militia and Iran's demands for the lifting of sanctions and the release of tens of billions of dollars of Iranian oil revenues frozen in foreign banks.

A senior Trump administration official told reporters an agreement would not be signed on Sunday, saying the Iranian system did not move fast enough.

But he outlined what he said were the latest contours of what was being negotiated.

The official, speaking on the condition of anonymity, said Iran had agreed "in principle" to open the Strait of Hormuz, in exchange for the United States lifting its naval blockade, and to dispose of Iran's highly enriched uranium.

He said the US understood Iran's Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei had endorsed the broad template of the deal.

There was no immediate confirmation from Iran or elaboration on what an "in principle" agreement meant.

The US official said the US envisioned first reopening the strait and lifting the US naval blockade.

That would "take that economic pressure out of the world economy, and then you negotiate the mechanism by which they will give up various parts of the nuclear programme, and yes, of course, we would contemplate some time limit," the official said.

He pushed back on suggestions that Iran has not accepted disposing of its stockpiled enriched uranium.

title.en: Madrid protesters decry rising rents and housing shortage
title.zh: 马德里抗议者谴责租金上涨和住房短缺

summary.en: Protesters in Madrid are voicing concerns over escalating rents and a severe housing shortage, issues exacerbated by increased demand from tourism and population growth due to immigration.
summary.zh: 马德里抗议者对租金上涨和严重的住房短缺表示担忧，这些问题因旅游业和移民带来的人口增长而加剧。

body.en:
Housing has long ranked among the top concerns in Spain, where demand has risen because of tourism and immigration-driven population growth.

Thousands of people marched through Spain's capital,  Madrid , on Sunday, protesting soaring rents, high home prices and a growing housing shortage.

Organizers said more than 100,000 people joined the march, while authorities put the figure at about 23,000.

The demonstration, organized by the Madrid Tenants' Union and backed by Spain's two main trade unions, comes despite recent action by Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez's government to tackle the housing crisis .

"Housing measures, although some are moving in the right direction, are advancing at a snail's pace, while the housing crisis is escalating rapidly," Unai Sordo, secretary general of the CCOO union, said.

Spain's central bank says that between 2021 and 2025, the number of new households grew faster than the number of new homes built, leading to a shortage of about 700,000 homes.

"More and more people are being forced into overcrowded conditions, having to live in shared rooms or even with other families," a spokesman for the tenants' union, Fernando de los Santos, told the AFP news agency.

According to the EU statistics agency Eurostat, housing costs rose nearly 13% year-on-year in 2025.

To help counter this, the government last month approved a new plan worth 7 billion euros ($8.23 billion) to build more public housing over the next four years. It also includes assistance for young renters and homebuyers.

Another key demand from protesters is a tougher government crackdown on tourist rentals .

Holiday homes have surged in city centers, outpacing hotel growth for years during Spain's tourism boom, but locals say the spread of holiday rentals is pushing up rents and property prices.

Authorities are now tightening rules as pressure mounts to protect housing for residents.

title.en: New Chinese surveillance leaves foreigners nowhere to hide
title.zh: 中国新的监控让外国人无处藏身

summary.en: A Chinese cybersecurity expert has revealed to DW details of China's new high-tech policing. From ski resort facial recognition to seats on a train, the system can track anyone and compile a "holistic profile."
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及真理、分辨与诚实。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
A Chinese cybersecurity expert has revealed to DW details of China's new high-tech policing. From ski resort facial recognition to seats on a train, the system can track anyone and compile a "holistic profile."

When a cybersecurity researcher known by the pseudonym NetAskari recently clicked on a tab labeled "Inquiry for journalist files" on an unsecured Chinese web dashboard, he expected to see a jumble of auto-generated mock data.

Instead, familiar faces popped up on the screen. It was a comprehensive database of almost every foreign journalist based in Beijing around 2021, including official passport photos taken at the entry/exit bureau, private cellphone numbers, visa details and dates of birth. He also found his own exact personal information lying dormant on this Chinese police watch list.

"It was more interesting than shocking," NetAskari told DW. "When you work as a journalist in China , you basically assume you are always on their radar. But what surprised me was simply how easy it was to access this highly sensitive system."

What NetAskari had stumbled upon is part modern China's emerging system of "holographic profiles."

He had unwittingly accessed a demonstration version of a remote tracking system designed for the Public Security Bureau in Zhangjiakou, the Hebei province city that hosted the 2022 Winter Olympics.

Though it was only a test panel, it was populated with real datasets, clearly outlining the trajectory of China's state surveillance machine, which is rapidly evolving from a network of simple street cameras into a data-fused, 24/7, predictive social control behemoth.

For years, China has operated the world's most extensive CCTV network. A massive initiative known as the "Xueliang" (Bright Eyes) project aims to merge these isolated islands of surveillance spread across the country.

But the data on the Zhangjiakou police dashboard shows the granular detail with which authorities can track an individual.

This system no longer relies solely on police cameras on street corners; it accurately records the specific train carriage and seat number a target occupies when arriving from Beijing or Shanghai, for example.

It even synchronizes photos taken by facial-recognition ticket gates at local ski resorts directly into its tracking mechanism. The movements of the researcher's acquaintances who recently skied in Zhangjiakou were precisely flagged and mapped out with detailed trajectories in the system.

"The idea is simply to process as much data as possible from as many sensors as possible in real time," the researcher noted.

The system logs daily behaviors like gasoline consumption, regular shopping locations and whether an individual frequently visits "petition areas."

body.zh: 一位中国网络安全专家向德国之声透露了中国新型高科技警务的细节。从滑雪场面部识别到火车座位，该系统可以跟踪任何人并编制“整体档案”。 当一位化名 NetAskari 的网络安全研究人员最近点击一个不安全的中文网络仪表板上标有“查询记者档案”的选项卡时，他预计会看到一堆自动生成的模拟数据。 取而代之的是，熟悉的面孔出现在屏幕上。这是一个综合数据库，包含 2021 年左右驻京的几乎所有外国记者，包括在出入境局拍摄的官方护照照片、私人手机号码、签证详细信息和出生日期。他还发现自己的确切个人信息隐藏在这份中国警方的监视名单上。 “这比令人震惊更有趣，”内特阿斯卡里告诉德国之声。 “当你在中国担任记者时，你基本上会认为你总是在他们的监视范围内。但令我惊讶的是访问这个高度敏感的系统是多么容易。” NetAskari 偶然发现的是现代中国新兴的“全息轮廓”系统的一部分。 他无意中访问了为主办 2022 年冬季奥运会的河北省张家口市公安局设计的远程跟踪系统演示版本。 虽然它只是一个测试面板，但它填充了真实的数据集，清楚地概述了中国国家监控机器的轨迹，该机器正在从简单的街道摄像头网络迅速演变为数据融合的、24/7、预测性的社会控制庞然大物。 多年来，中国运营着世界上最广泛的闭路电视网络。一项名为“雪亮”（明亮的眼睛）项目的大规模倡议旨在合并这些分布在全国各地的监视孤岛。 但张家口警方仪表板上的数据显示了当局可以追踪个人的详细信息。 该系统不再仅仅依赖于街角的警察摄像头；例如，它可以准确记录目标从北京或上海抵达时所乘坐的具体火车车厢和座位号。 它甚至将当地滑雪场的面部识别检票口拍摄的照片直接同步到其跟踪机制中。研究人员最近在张家口滑雪的熟人的动作被精确标记，并在系统中绘制出详细的轨迹。 研究人员指出：“这个想法只是实时处理来自尽可能多的传感器的尽可能多的数据。” 该系统会记录日常行为，例如汽油消耗、常规购物地点以及个人是否经常访问“请愿区”。 这种大规模的数据融合工作......

reflection.en: This story draws attention to truth, discernment, and honest speech. Philippians 4:8 reminds us to meet sharp headlines with discernment and truthful speech, asking how faithful people can respond with wisdom instead of noise.
reflection.zh: 这则新闻让人想到真理、分辨与诚实。Philippians 4:8提醒我们，在快速变化的新闻里，仍要以分辨与诚实表达来回应，并学习用祷告与分辨代替情绪化判断。

verse.textEn: Whatever is true, whatever is noble, whatever is right, whatever is pure, whatever is lovely, whatever is admirable — think about such things.
verse.textZh: 凡是真实的、可敬的、公义的、清洁的、可爱的、有美名的，这些事你们都要思念。

title.en: Displaced Ukrainians risk home seizure under Russian law
title.zh: 流离失所的乌克兰人面临俄罗斯法律下的房屋没收风险

summary.en: Russia is tightening control over property in occupied Ukrainian territories, requiring owners to register under Russian law. Many Ukrainians say returning to do so would put their safety and freedom at risk.
summary.zh: 俄罗斯正在加强对被占乌克兰领土财产的控制，要求业主根据俄罗斯法律进行登记。许多流离失所的乌克兰人表示，如果他们返回办理登记，将危及他们的安全和自由。

body.en:
Russia is tightening control over property in occupied Ukrainian territories, requiring owners to register under Russian law. Many Ukrainians say returning to do so would put their safety and freedom at risk.

Russian authorities have granted owners of land and real estate in the Russian-occupied territories of Ukraine until July 1, 2026 to claim ownership of any property originally registered under Ukrainian law.

But to re-register their property in the Russian land registry, owners have to appear in person and present a Russian passport as proof of their identity — an impossibility for many Ukrainians.

"It breaks my heart," said Lyudmila (name changed.) "I built my whole life there. My business was bombed. I had to leave behind everything I held dear. I had hoped they would at least let me keep my apartment."

In 2022, she fled the Zaporizhzhia region to the Ukrainian capital, Kyiv, to escape the Russian occupation . But she continued to pay the utility bills for her home. "At first, a neighbor kept an eye on the apartment, and after that my ex-husband did. Then I decided that starting with New Year's Day, I would stop paying the bills. I don't know if I was even right to pay them in the first place," Lyudmyla told DW. "I am waiting for my city to be liberated."

Until then, she doesn't intend to go home to re-register her apartment with the occupying authorities. "First of all, I don't want to see the occupiers because I was there and I know what these people are like. And I don't want to lose years of my life and get stressed. Second, I don't even know if they would let me in."

Russian occupiers started seizing the homes of Ukrainians in occupied territories in 2014. Seven years, in 2021, the authorities of the self-proclaimed Donetsk People's Republic began classifying abandoned residential properties as "ownerless." These can now be sold or seized by "courts."

In 2024, the occupying authorities went a step further and defined as "ownerless" apartments or buildings that have been vacant for more than a year, for which no utility bills have been paid, and whose owners do not appear in Russian land registries. They justified the decision by saying that the security of the property itself was at risk. At the end of 2025, this approach was legalized at the federal level in Russia. "Ownerless" apartments can now be transferred to Russian citizens.

It's almost impossible to determine how many apartments Russian authorities have already taken in the occupied Ukrainian territories. Last August, the head of Russia's Federal Service for State Registration, Oleg Skufinskiy, announced that there were around 550,000 "ownerless" properties in the occupied Ukrainian territories; 13,000 residential units in the occupied Ukrainian city of...
body.zh: 俄罗斯正在加强对乌克兰被占领土财产的控制，要求业主根据俄罗斯法律进行登记。许多乌克兰人表示，返回乌克兰将使他们的安全和自由面临风险。 俄罗斯当局已允许俄罗斯占领的乌克兰领土上的土地和房地产所有者在 2026 年 7 月 1 日之前对最初根据乌克兰法律登记的任何财产拥有所有权。 但要在俄罗斯土地登记处重新登记其财产，业主必须亲自到场并出示俄罗斯护照作为身份证明——这对许多乌克兰人来说是不可能的。 “这让我心碎，”柳德米拉（化名）说道，“我在那里度过了一生。我的生意遭到了轰炸。我不得不放弃我所珍视的一切。我曾希望他们至少能让我保留我的公寓。” 2022年，她逃离扎波罗热地区前往乌克兰首都基辅，以躲避俄罗斯的占领。但她继续支付家里的水电费。柳德米拉告诉德国之声：“一开始，邻居一直在监视着公寓，后来我的前夫也监视着。然后我决定从元旦开始，我将停止支付账单。我什至不知道我一开始支付账单是否正确。” “我正在等待我的城市被解放。” 在那之前，她不打算回家向占领当局重新登记她的公寓。 “首先，我不想看到占领者，因为我在那里，我知道这些人是什么样的。我不想浪费生命并承受压力。其次，我什至不知道他们是否会让我进去。” 俄罗斯占领者从 2014 年开始没收被占领土上的乌克兰人的房屋。七年后，即 2021 年，自称为顿涅茨克人民共和国的当局开始将废弃的住宅物业归类为“无主”。这些现在可以被“法院”出售或扣押。 2024年，占领当局更进一步，将“无主”公寓或空置超过一年、未支付水电费且业主未在俄罗斯土地登记处登记的建筑物定义为“无主”公寓或建筑物。他们为这一决定辩护称，财产本身的安全面临风险。 2025 年底，这种方法在俄罗斯联邦层面合法化。 “无主”公寓现在可以转让给俄罗斯公民。 几乎不可能确定俄罗斯当局已经在被占领的乌克兰领土上征用了多少公寓。去年 8 月，俄罗斯联邦国家登记局局长奥列格·斯库芬斯基 (Oleg Skufinskiy) 宣布，被占领的乌克兰领土上约有 55 万处“无主”财产；被占领的乌克兰城市 13,000 个住宅单元

reflection.en: This news highlights the profound injustice faced by displaced Ukrainians, who are forced to choose between their safety and their homes. The prophetic call for rulers to administer justice and protect the robbed and the vulnerable echoes deeply in such situations. It reminds us of the moral responsibility to defend those who are dispossessed and cannot...
reflection.zh: 这则新闻凸显了流离失所的乌克兰人所面临的深刻不公，他们被迫在自身安全和家园之间做出选择。先知呼吁统治者施行公义，从压迫者手中解救被抢夺之人，这在当前情境中引起了深刻共鸣。它提醒我们有道德责任去捍卫那些被剥夺财产且无法自卫的人。

verse.textEn: Do what is just and right. Rescue from the hand of the oppressor the one who has been robbed.
verse.textZh: 你们要施行公平和公义，拯救被抢夺的脱离欺压人的手。

title.en: 'I shouted run': Witness recalls moment of China's worst mine disaster in years
title.zh: “我大喊快跑”：目击者回忆中国多年来最严重矿难发生瞬间

summary.en: A recent mining accident in China has been described as the country's deadliest since 2009, resulting in a significant loss of life. A witness recalled shouting for people to run during the incident.
summary.zh: 中国最近发生的一起矿难被描述为自2009年以来该国最致命的事故，造成了重大人员伤亡。一名目击者回忆在事故发生时曾大喊让人快跑。

body.en:
As emergency rescuers undertook a major rescue operation after Saturday's mining accident that killed at least 82 people in northern China, a wounded survivor said he heard no sound but smelled sulphur when the explosion happened.

"I didn't hear any sound at all, but then a cloud of smoke appeared," miner Wang Yong said.

"When I smelled it, it was the smell of sulphur like when people set off firecrackers. When the smoke came down, I shouted for people to run," he said.

"After more than an hour, I came to on my own, and then I woke up the person next to me" and got out, he told Chinese broadcaster CCTV.

The blast at the Liushenyu shaft in Shanxi province was the country's worst mining disaster in nearly two decades, with 247 workers underground at the time, according to Chinese media.

Hundreds of rescuers have rushed to the site, with medical teams taking 128 people to the hospital as of Saturday evening (local time), loaded into ambulances and carried on stretchers. Two people still remain missing.

Agence France-Presse journalists saw police blocking the road leading to the mine late Saturday, allowing only authorised vehicles to enter.

Helmeted rescuers took turns descending into the shaft overnight to look for the two missing workers, state media reported.

"As long as there is hope, we will make every possible effort," one rescuer told Xinhua news agency.

Chinese authorities launched an investigation into the blast, the worst since 2009 when 108 people were killed in a mine explosion in northeastern Heilongjiang province.

Preliminary findings showed the company operating the mine had committed "serious illegal violations", authorities told a press conference.

"Those found responsible will be severely punished in accordance with laws and regulations," they added.

A person "responsible for" the company involved had been "placed under control in accordance with the law", Xinhua reported.

The State Council, China's cabinet, ordered nationwide "tough crackdowns on illegal and unlawful activities", including the falsification of safety data, unclear headcounts of underground workers and illegal contracting.

Shanxi, one of China's poorer provinces, is the centre of the country's coal-mining industry.

Mine safety in China has improved in recent decades, but accidents still occur in an industry where safety protocols are often lax and regulations are vague.

In 2023, a collapse at an open-pit coal mine in the northern Inner Mongolia region killed 53 people.

China is the world's top consumer of coal and the largest greenhouse gas emitter, despite installing renewable energy capacity at record speed.

Coal miners in the sleepy Chinese county of Qinyuan sometimes dine at Zhang's skewer eatery, especially on payday, and the accident has left...
body.zh: 周六，中国北方发生了导致至少 82 人死亡的矿难，紧急救援人员在开展重大救援行动时，一名受伤的幸存者表示，爆炸发生时他没有听到任何声音，但闻到了硫磺的味道。 “我根本没有听到任何声音，但随后出现了一团烟雾。”矿工王勇说。 “当我闻到的时候，那是硫磺的味道，就像人们放鞭炮时一样。当烟雾降下时，我大声喊叫人们快跑，”他说。 他告诉中国中央电视台，“一个多小时后，我自己醒了过来，然后我叫醒了旁边的人”，然后下了车。 据中国媒体报道，山西省六神峪竖井爆炸是该国近二十年来最严重的矿难，当时井下有 247 名工人。 截至周六晚间（当地时间），数百名救援人员已赶赴现场，医疗队已将 128 人送往医院，并装上救护车并用担架抬上。目前仍有两人失踪。 法新社记者周六晚看到警察封锁了通往矿井的道路，只允许经过授权的车辆进入。 据官方媒体报道，戴着头盔的救援人员连夜轮流进入竖井寻找两名失踪的工人。 “只要有希望，我们就会尽一切努力，”一名救援人员告诉新华社。 中国当局对这起爆炸展开调查，这是自2009年黑龙江省东北部矿井爆炸造成108人死亡以来最严重的一次。 当局在新闻发布会上表示，初步调查结果显示，该矿运营公司存在“严重违法行为”。 他们补充说：“对相关责任人，将依法依规予以严厉处罚。” 据新华社报道，涉事公司一名“负责人”已被“依法控制”。 中国国务院下令在全国范围内“严厉打击违法违规行为”，包括伪造安全数据、井下工人人数不明和非法承包等。 山西是中国较贫困的省份之一，也是全国煤炭开采业的中心。 近几十年来，中国的矿山安全有所改善，但安全规程往往松懈、法规模糊的行业中事故仍然时有发生。 2023年，内蒙古北部地区一座露天煤矿发生塌方，造成53人死亡。 尽管中国以创纪录的速度安装可再生能源产能，但它仍然是世界上最大的煤炭消费国和最大的温室气体排放国。 在中国寂静的沁源县，煤矿工人有时会在张的烤串店吃饭，尤其是在发薪日，事故已经发生……

reflection.en: The news of a devastating mine disaster brings profound sorrow, reminding us of the fragility of life and the pain of sudden loss. In moments of such tragedy, we hold onto the promise that one day, all tears will be wiped away, and death, mourning, crying, and pain will be no more. This hope offers solace to those grieving and a vision of a future free from...
reflection.zh: 这场毁灭性的矿难消息带来了深切的悲痛，提醒我们生命的脆弱和突如其来的损失所带来的痛苦。在这样的悲剧中，我们紧紧抓住一个应许：有一天，所有的眼泪都将被擦去，死亡、悲伤、哭泣和痛苦将不复存在。这个盼望为那些悲伤的人带来慰藉，并描绘了一个没有此类苦难的未来。

verse.textEn: He will wipe every tear from their eyes. There will be no more death or mourning or crying or pain.
verse.textZh: 神要擦去他们一切的眼泪；不再有死亡，也不再有悲哀、哭号、疼痛。

title.en: 'He thrives on controversy': The past and possible future of Israel's 'TikTok minister'
title.zh: “靠争议而兴盛”：以色列“TikTok部长”的过去与未来

summary.en: Itamar Ben-Gvir, known as Israel's 'TikTok minister' for his controversial style, has reached the highest echelons of Israeli politics. Despite his rapid rise, analysts suggest his future in this position may be short-lived.
summary.zh: 伊塔马尔·本-格维尔因其富有争议的风格而被戏称为以色列的“TikTok部长”，他已晋升至以色列政坛的最高层。尽管他迅速崛起，但分析人士认为他在此职位上的未来可能不会长久。

body.en:
Far-right Israeli national security minister Itamar Ben-Gvir was once again in the headlines this week after a video of him taunting detained activists went viral , drawing rebuke from world leaders and his own prime minister.

However, it arguably isn't the most notorious footage featuring the man some Israelis refer to as the 'TikTok minister'.

In November 1995, just weeks before then Israeli prime minister Yitzak Rabin was assassinated by an ultranationalist Jew opposed to peace talks with Palestinians, a teenage Ben-Gvir appeared on live television holding an emblem stolen from the prime minister's Cadillac and saying: "We got to his car, and we'll get to him, too."

Ben-Gvir has never been accused of any direct responsibility for Rabin's death. But he and the extremist who did kill him moved in broadly similar ideological circles, fiercely against the Oslo Accords that Rabin signed.

The two incidents are also only the bookends of a prolific array of provocative videos the 50-year-old has become known for over the years.

In August last year, he posted videos of himself taunting popular Palestinian prisoner Marwan Barghouti in his jail cell. Several months later, footage emerged of him mocking a previous group of captured Global Sumud Flotilla activists and accusing them of supporting terrorism.

Ran Porat from The Australian Centre for Jewish Civilisation at Monash University described Ben-Gvir as someone who "operates by creating these viral moments of 'this is Jewish power'."

"He thrives on controversy ... He thrives on these videos that depict him as powerful," said Porat, who is also a research associate for the Australia/Israel & Jewish Affairs Council.

However, Porat and other experts don't think Ben-Gvir is likely to remain in government after the upcoming Israeli elections, even if he might be increasingly popular among the nation's hard-right edge.

Ben-Gvir's televised 1995 threat to the prime minister took place when he was a member of a right-wing youth movement opposing the mid-1990s peace negotiations between Israel and the Palestine Liberation Organization.

In his younger years, he faced dozens of charges relating to anti-Arab incitement, support of proscribed organisations, disturbing the peace and other public-order offences, but was acquitted of most. He has eight criminal convictions, including support for a terrorist organisation and incitement to racism, one of which related to him carrying a sign reading "Expel the Arab enemy" in 2007.

He is a long-time settler in the occupied West Bank and, while working as a defence attorney before entering parliament, represented many Jewish settlers accused of violence against Palestinians.

Although he has been active in Israeli parliamentary politics...
body.zh: 以色列极右翼国家安全部长伊塔马尔·本-格维尔本周再次成为头条新闻，此前他嘲笑被拘留的活动人士的视频在网上疯传，引起了世界领导人和他自己的总理的谴责。 然而，这可能不是一些以色列人称之为“TikTok 部长”的最臭名昭著的视频。 1995 年 11 月，就在时任以色列总理伊扎克·拉宾 (Yitzak Rabin) 被一名反对与巴勒斯坦人和谈的极端民族主义犹太人暗杀的几周前，十几岁的本·格维尔 (Ben-Gvir) 出现在电视直播中，手里拿着从总理的凯迪拉克上偷来的徽章，并说道：“我们上了他的车，我们也会找到他。” 本-格维尔从未被指控对拉宾之死负有任何直接责任。但他和杀害他的极端分子在大致相似的意识形态圈子里活动，强烈反对拉宾签署的《奥斯陆协议》。 这两起事件也只是这位 50 岁的人多年来出名的一系列大量挑衅性视频的书挡。 去年八月，他发布了自己在牢房中嘲笑受欢迎的巴勒斯坦囚犯马尔万·巴尔古提的视频。几个月后，视频出现，显示他嘲笑先前被俘的全球苏姆德船队活动分子，并指责他们支持恐怖主义。 莫纳什大学澳大利亚犹太文明中心的兰·波拉特 (Ran Porat) 将本·格维尔描述为“通过创造‘这是犹太力量’的病毒式时刻来运作的人”。 “他在争议中茁壮成长……他在这些描绘他强大的视频中茁壮成长，”波拉特说，他也是澳大利亚/以色列和犹太事务委员会的研究员。 然而，波拉特和其他专家认为，本-格维尔在即将到来的以色列选举后不太可能继续留在政府，即使他可能在该国的极右翼边缘中越来越受欢迎。 1995 年，本-格维尔在电视上对总理发出威胁，当时他是反对 90 年代中期以色列与巴勒斯坦解放组织之间和平谈判的右翼青年运动的成员。 在他年轻的时候，他面临数十项与反阿拉伯煽动、支持被禁组织、扰乱和平和其他公共秩序犯罪有关的指控，但大多数罪名被无罪释放。 他有八项刑事定罪，包括支持恐怖组织和煽动种族主义，其中一项与他在 2007 年举着“驱逐阿拉伯敌人”的牌子有关。 他是被占领的约旦河西岸的长期定居者，在进入议会之前担任辩护律师，曾代表许多被指控对巴勒斯坦人实施暴力的犹太定居者。 尽管他一直活跃于以色列议会政治......

reflection.en: A leader who "thrives on controversy" often builds a platform on division rather than unity. While such an approach might lead to a rapid ascent, the wisdom of Scripture suggests that a foundation built on pride and contention is ultimately unstable. True leadership, grounded in humility and seeking the common good, fosters lasting influence and peace.
reflection.zh: 一个“靠争议而兴盛”的领导者，其平台往往建立在分裂而非团结之上。虽然这种方式可能带来快速的崛起，但圣经的智慧指出，建立在骄傲和纷争之上的根基最终是不稳固的。真正以谦卑为本、寻求共同利益的领导力，才能培养持久的影响力与和平。

verse.textEn: Pride goes before destruction, a haughty spirit before a fall.
verse.textZh: 骄傲在败坏以先；狂心在跌倒之前。

body.en:
Exclusive: BHP once dubbed climate change an ‘existential’ threat. But leaked documents show it has backtracked on decarbonisation at a vast network of mines

Temperature records tumbled. Frail, ill and elderly people died in their hundreds.

In a city not built for heat, trains were brought to a halt. Railway lines threatened to buckle and sagging power lines caused spot fires along the tracks.

Across the channel, Belgium, the Netherlands and Germany also hit record temperatures.

During the hottest week in late July, the then global chief executive of one of the world’s worst polluters was preparing to take the stage at a high-profile London event.

BHP’s Andrew Mackenzie stood before a collection of Britain’s most powerful – lords, MPs and diplomats – and gave a climate speech that made the world take notice.

Mackenzie warned that the world’s dependence on fossil fuels was causing risks that “could be existential”.

Global heating was indisputable, he said, and would have catastrophic consequences.

Here was one of the most powerful corporate leaders in the world making an impassioned call to arms on the problem his company helped cause. Mackenzie said global warming required the “biggest global mobilisation since World War II”.

The company later pledged to reduce emissions from its operations, largely from energy and diesel use at its mines, by 30% by 2030 and had already set a goal to reach net zero emissions by 2050. It also sought to curtail indirect emissions – from the use of its iron ore and coal by others – which at that stage were the equivalent of pollution from roughly 126m cars.

Six years after Mackenzie’s speech, long after he had left the company, senior BHP executives were presented with an internal memo dated May 2025.

The memo was about the company’s plans to decarbonise a significant contributor to its global emissions: the vast network of Pilbara mines, power plants, trains and diesel truck fleets that make up its Western Australian iron ore division.

The urgency for BHP to source renewables had “diminished”, it said. BHP was now claiming the plan it had devised to hit net zero in the Pilbara by 2050 had a “low probability of success”.

“To preserve optionality … alternate pathway decisions have been preserved and will continue to be assessed.”

The memo canvassed options that would massively delay key decarbonisation projects.

A huge wind and solar project, big enough to power roughly 150,000 homes, would be delayed, the memo said.

BHP then contemplated three “scenarios” that would put off the electrification of its highly polluting truck and rail fleets.

The first option, described as the “central” or “FY35 deployment” case, would push the rollout of battery-electric trucks and trains as far back as 2035 – a...
body.zh: 独家：必和必拓曾将气候变化称为“生存”威胁。但泄露的文件显示，该公司在大型矿山网络的脱碳问题上出现了倒退。 气温记录大幅下降。数百名体弱、患病和老人死亡。 在一个不适合炎热的城市里，火车停了下来。铁路线有弯曲的危险，电线下垂导致铁轨沿线发生局部火灾。 英吉利海峡对岸的比利时、荷兰和德国也创下了创纪录的气温。 在七月下旬最热的一周里，世界上污染最严重的公司之一的时任全球首席执行官正准备在一场备受瞩目的伦敦活动上登台。 必和必拓的安德鲁·麦肯齐 (Andrew Mackenzie) 站在英国最有权势的贵族、议员和外交官面前，发表了引起全世界关注的气候演讲。 麦肯齐警告说，世界对化石燃料的依赖正在造成“可能影响生存”的风险。 他说，全球变暖是无可争议的，并将带来灾难性后果。 这是世界上最有权势的企业领导人之一，他慷慨激昂地呼吁解决他的公司造成的问题。麦肯齐表示，全球变暖需要“二战以来最大规模的全球动员”。 该公司后来承诺，到 2030 年将其运营排放量（主要来自矿山的能源和柴油使用）减少 30%，并已设定到 2050 年实现净零排放的目标。该公司还寻求减少间接排放量（其他公司使用铁矿石和煤炭产生的排放量），该排放量在当时相当于约 1.26 亿辆汽车的污染。 麦肯齐发表演讲六年后，也就是他离开公司很久之后，必和必拓高级管理人员收到了一份日期为 2025 年 5 月的内部备忘录。 该备忘录涉及该公司计划对其全球排放的一个重要贡献者进行脱碳：构成其西澳大利亚铁矿石部门的庞大的皮尔巴拉矿山、发电厂、火车和柴油卡车车队网络。 必和必拓表示，采购可再生能源的紧迫性已经“减弱”。必和必拓现在声称，其制定的到 2050 年皮尔巴拉地区实现净零排放的计划“成功的可能性很低”。 “为了保留选择性……替代途径的决定已被保留并将继续评估。” 该备忘录探讨了将大幅推迟关键脱碳项目的选项。 备忘录称，一个足以为大约 15 万户家庭供电的大型风能和太阳能项目将被推迟。 必和必拓随后考虑了三种“情景”，以推迟其高污染卡车和铁路车队的电气化。 第一个选项被称为“中央”或“2035 财年部署”案例，将推动电池电动卡车和火车的推出最早可追溯到 2035 年——a...

title.en: Moment of gas explosion at China coal mine
title.zh: 中国煤矿瓦斯爆炸瞬间

summary.en: Officials report that at least 82 people have died and two are missing following a gas explosion at a coal mine in northern China on Sunday.
summary.zh: 官员称，周日中国北方一煤矿发生瓦斯爆炸，造成至少82人死亡，另有两人失踪。

body.en:
At least 82 people have been killed and at least two are missing after a gas explosion at a coal mine in northern China on Sunday, officials say.

Surveillance footage aired by state media on Monday showed the moment of the blast from inside Liushenyu Coal Mine in Shanxi province.

The incident is the worst mining disaster in China since 2009, and Chinese President Xi Jinping said no effort must be spared in the search and rescue operation.

The cause of the gas explosion has not yet been revealed, but state media reported that the levels of carbon monoxide in the mine were found to have "exceeded limits".

body.zh: 官员称，周日中国北方一煤矿发生瓦斯爆炸，已造成至少 82 人死亡，至少两人失踪。 官方媒体周一播出的监控录像显示了山西省六神峪煤矿内部爆炸的瞬间。 此次事故是2009年以来中国最严重的矿难，中国国家主席习近平表示，必须全力以赴开展搜救工作。 瓦斯爆炸的原因尚未公布，但官方媒体报道称，矿井中的一氧化碳含量被发现“超出限度”。 朝鲜女子足球队在韩国比赛，这是近八年来朝鲜运动员首次跨越边境。 巴基斯坦称其袭击了“军事和恐怖主义基础设施”，但联合国和受害者家属否认了这一说法。 官员们表示，尽管有攀登禁令，该组织仍在攀登活火山。 5 月 4 日，西爪哇省茂物市的一处豪华露营设施被汹涌的洪流摧毁。 马来西亚沙巴州发生火灾，烧毁了约 1,000 所房屋，导致数千人流离失所。 两岁大的狼 Neukgu 从大田市动物园逃跑引起了全国关注。 菲律宾总统要求任何质疑他健康状况的人都和他一起去健身房。 韩国流行歌星防弹少年团 (BTS) 在韩国拉开了马拉松世界巡演的序幕，向他们的新专辑《阿里郎》致敬。 经过近四年的中断后，这些巨星将于周四在首尔开始他们最盛大的巡演，这也是韩国流行音乐历史上规模最大的巡演。 敏昂莱主持了就任总统之前在缅甸的最后一次阅兵。 随着伊朗战争继续在全球范围内产生冲击波，司机们在缅甸的加油站排队几个小时。 BBC 新闻亚洲商业记者 Suranajana Tewari 向走上马尼拉街头的人们发表讲话。 周六，预计将有约 26 万粉丝观看 BTS 自 2022 年以来的首次共同表演。 中部城市大田的一家汽车零部件工厂发生大火，造成 11 人死亡、数十人受伤。 克什米尔高级领导人法鲁克·阿卜杜拉在事件发生后逃脱，没有受伤，嫌疑人已被拘留。 日本市川市动物园的一只年轻日本猕猴在网上疯传，视频显示它正在玩动物园管理员为了安慰它而送给它的毛绒玩具。 嫌疑人因多项盗窃罪被通缉，最终在曼谷郊区的一座寺庙外被捕。 法院即将对尹锡烈叛乱案作出判决。 BBC 的阿鲁诺迪·穆克哈吉 (Arunoday Mukharji) 解释了为什么印度需要利用这一势头。 曼谷购物中心的拉克希米女神神社已成为年轻人的聚集地。

reflection.en: In the wake of such a devastating loss of life, our hearts ache for all affected by this tragedy. Revelation 21:4 offers a profound hope, reminding us of a future where God will wipe away every tear and death will be no more. This promise provides comfort and a vision of ultimate peace beyond present suffering.
reflection.zh: 面对如此毁灭性的生命损失，我们的心为所有受这场悲剧影响的人而痛。启示录21:4提供了一个深刻的盼望，提醒我们有一个未来，雅伟将擦去所有的眼泪，死亡也将不复存在。这个应许带来了安慰，并描绘了一个超越当前苦难的终极平安的异象。

title.en: Anger grows after China's deadliest coal mining disaster in years
title.zh: 中国多年来最致命煤矿灾难后，民众怒火中烧

summary.en: Public anger and calls for accountability are rising on China's internet following the country's deadliest coal mining disaster in years, with people questioning the circumstances of the tragedy.
summary.zh: 中国多年来最严重的煤矿灾难发生后，中国受到严格管控的互联网上，民众的愤怒情绪日益高涨，人们呼吁伸张正义，并质疑事故是如何发生的。

body.en:
Anger is growing over alleged safety violations in the wake of China's worst mining disaster in more than 15 years.

At least 82 people were killed and more than 120 injured after an explosion on Friday at the Liushenyu coal mine in Shanxi province, the heart of China's huge mining industry.

For many in China, the tragedy harks back to the 2000s, a period of regular, deadly coal mining disasters, which is widely thought to have been left in the past.

Those concerns are now reignited and playing out on China's tightly-controlled internet, with people calling for justice and questioning how this happened: "It's so heartbreaking, so many precious lives lost. When will we truly put safety first?"

Authorities say the cause of the disaster is still under investigation, but initial findings show Tongzhou Group, the company operating the privately-owned coal mine had committed "serious illegal violations".

At a news conference on Saturday, they pledged to conduct a "rigorous" investigation and "severely punish" those found responsible.

Tongzhou Group has not made a public statement so far, and the BBC has been unable to reach them for comment.

China's state media reported that the people running Tongzhou Group have been put under "control measures", though it's unclear what that means. The company has also been ordered to halt work at all four coal mines it currently operates in Shanxi province.

Authorities have not specified the safety violations they discovered at Liushenyu coal mine. State media, however, highlighted various issues at the site.

Reports claim that some workers did not bring mandatory tracking devices into the mines, and blueprints provided by the Liushenyu coal mine to authorities did not match the conditions at the mine, complicating rescue efforts.

State media also reported that the number of people in the mine at the time of the explosion was double that listed in the company's official count.

"Why are there more than 100 unregistered workers appearing out of the blue?" a Weibo user questioned. "Was it to exceed production limits? To reduce costs? Or to conceal the number of workers during an accident?"

Tongzhou Group has reportedly received two administrative penalties in 2025 for safety violations. In 2024 the Liushenyu mine was named by the Chinese National Mine Safety Administration in a nationwide list of coal mines with "severe hazards", state media reported.

"This incident not only exposes the superficiality of local daily supervision and the low cost of violations, leading to repeated violations by the company," another Weibo user wrote.

This is among hundreds of thousands of posts and comments discussing the tragedy.

In the case of previous disasters, criticism of the government has usually been scrubbed off the...
body.zh: 在中国发生15年来最严重的矿难之后，人们对涉嫌安全违规的愤怒日益高涨。 周五，中国庞大采矿业的中心山西省六神峪煤矿发生爆炸，造成至少 82 人死亡、120 多人受伤。 对许多中国人来说，这场悲剧让人回想起2000年代，那段时期经常发生致命的煤矿灾难，但人们普遍认为那段时期已经成为过去。 这些担忧现在重新燃起，并在中国严格控制的互联网上上演，人们呼吁伸张正义，并质疑这件事是如何发生的：“这太令人心碎了，这么多宝贵的生命失去了。我们什么时候才能真正把安全放在第一位？” 当局表示，事故原因仍在调查中，但初步调查结果显示，经营该私营煤矿的通州集团存在“严重违法行为”。 在周六的新闻发布会上，他们承诺进行“严格”调查并“严厉惩罚”责任人。 截至目前，通州集团尚未发表公开声明，BBC 也未能联系到他们置评。 中国官方媒体报道称，通州集团的经营者已受到“控制措施”，但尚不清楚这意味着什么。该公司还被勒令停止其目前在山西省运营的所有四个煤矿的工作。 当局没有具体说明他们在六神峪煤矿发现的安全违规行为。然而，官方媒体强调了现场的各种问题。 报道称，一些工人没有将强制追踪设备带入矿井，而且六神峪煤矿向当局提供的蓝图与矿井条件不符，使救援工作变得复杂。 官方媒体还报道称，爆炸时矿井内的人数是该公司官方统计人数的两倍。 “为什么突然出现100多名未登记工人？”有微博网友质疑。 “是为了超出产量限制？为了降低成本？还是为了隐瞒事故发生时的工人人数？” 据悉，通州集团2025年已因安全违规两次受到行政处罚。据官方媒体报道，2024年，六神峪煤矿被中国国家矿山安全管理局列入全国“严重危险”煤矿名单。 另一位微博用户写道：“这起事件不仅暴露了当地日常监管的肤浅和违法成本之低，导致该公司屡屡违法。” 这是讨论这场悲剧的数十万条帖子和评论之一。 在以前发生的灾难中，对政府的批评通常都会被消除......

reflection.en: When tragedy strikes, especially in preventable circumstances, a deep human longing for justice emerges. The public's call for answers and accountability echoes the ancient prophetic cry for righteousness to flow powerfully and continuously, ensuring that such suffering is not in vain.
reflection.zh: 当悲剧发生，尤其是在本可避免的情况下，人们内心深处对正义的渴望便会浮现。公众对答案和问责的呼吁，与古老先知对公义如大水般奔流不息的呐喊遥相呼应，确保此类苦难不会白费。

verse.textEn: Let justice roll on like a river, righteousness like a never-failing stream!

title.en: First Hong Kong astronaut launches into space onboard Chinese mission
title.zh: 首位香港宇航员搭乘中国任务升入太空

summary.en: The 43-year-old police officer and mother of three serves as the team's payload scientist.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自中国栏目的新闻，重点涉及智慧、知识与追求真理。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
A Hong Kong astronaut has been launched into space for the first time, aboard China's Shenzhou-23 spacecraft.

Li Jiaying, a 43-year-old police officer and mother of three, serves as the payload scientist in the three-member crew who made their way to China's Tiangong space station on Sunday night.

At least one member of the crew will spend a full year in orbit as part of a key experiment. Authorities will determine who that will be at a later date.

The mission is the latest in China's ambitious space program to send humans to the moon by 2030. It comes amid an accelerating race with the US, which is looking to achieve a crewed lunar landing by 2028.

The Shenzhou-23 is tasked with studying the effects of microgravity on the human body, among many experiments.

Apart from Li, the two other astronauts on the mission are Zhu Yangzhu, a 39-year-old space engineer and Zhang Zhiyuan, a 39-year-old former air force pilot.

Large crowds waved Chinese flags as the rocket launched from the north-west Gobi desert on the Long March 2-F rocket at 23:08 local (15:08 GMT) Sunday. A few hours later, it docked on the Tiangong space station.

Hong Kong Chief Executive John Lee said Li's inclusion in the mission was a "historic" moment.

Li said she was inspired by Yang Liwei, the first person sent to space by China's space programme.

As she made her way to the launch on Sunday, Li said, according to state broadcaster CCTV: "How high our Chinese spacecraft flies, that's how high we can hold our heads high".

Stories of successful Hong Kong figures like Li could help Chinese authorities stir patriotism, especially among the youth, analysts told BBC Chinese.

Since 2021, China has been sending astronauts to its Tiangong space station on six-month stays.

The year-long stay will be among the longest in history, just shy of the 14-month record set by a Russian cosmonaut Valery Polyakov in 1995.

"A year in orbit pushes both hardware and humans into a different operational regime compared with the shorter Shenzhou missions of the programme's earlier phases," Richard de Grijs, an astrophysicist and professor at Macquarie University in Australia, told AFP news agency.

This shows how China is building its expertise in long stays in space as well as deep space exploration, de Grijs said.

In 2024, China's Chang'e-6 craft recovered rock samples from the far side of the Moon for the first time and brought them back to Earth.

Later this year, China is set to mount an orbital test flight for its Mengzhou spacecraft, which is designed to carry astronauts to the moon.
body.zh: 一名香港宇航员乘坐中国神舟二十三号飞船首次进入太空。 李嘉莹是一名 43 岁的警官，也是三个孩子的母亲，她是周日晚前往中国天宫空间站的三名宇航员中的有效载荷科学家。 作为一项关键实验的一部分，至少一名宇航员将在轨道上度过一整年。当局将在稍后确定谁是该人。 此次任务是中国雄心勃勃的太空计划中的最新一项，该计划旨在于 2030 年将人类送上月球。此次任务正值中国与美国加速竞赛之际，美国希望在 2028 年实现载人登月。 神舟二十三号的任务之一是研究微重力对人体的影响。 除了李之外，执行任务的另外两名宇航员是39岁的太空工程师朱杨柱和39岁的前空军飞行员张志远。 周日当地时间 23 点 08 分（格林威治标准时间 15 点 08 分），当长征二号 F 火箭从西北戈壁沙漠发射升空时，大批人群挥舞着中国国旗。几个小时后，它停靠在天宫空间站上。 香港行政长官李家超表示，李克强的出访是一个“历史性”时刻。 李说，她受到了中国航天计划第一人杨利伟的启发。 据国家电视台中央电视台报道，周日，李在前往发射场时说道：“我们中国的航天器飞得有多高，我们就能昂首挺胸”。 分析人士告诉英国广播公司中文网，像李这样的香港成功人士的故事可以帮助中国当局激发爱国主义，特别是在年轻人中。 自2021年以来，中国一直在向天宫空间站派遣宇航员，为期六个月。 这次停留长达一年的时间将是历史上最长的停留时间之一，仅略低于俄罗斯宇航员瓦列里·波利亚科夫 (Valery Polyakov) 在 1995 年创下的 14 个月的纪录。 澳大利亚麦考瑞大学天体物理学家兼教授理查德·德·格里克斯对法新社表示：“与该计划早期阶段较短的神舟任务相比，在轨一年的时间将硬件和人类推入不同的运行状态。” 德格里斯说，这表明中国正在如何建立长期太空停留和深空探索方面的专业知识。 2024年，中国嫦娥六号飞船首次从月球背面回收岩石样本并将其带回地球。 今年晚些时候，中国将对其孟州飞船进行轨道试飞，该飞船旨在将宇航员送上月球。

reflection.en: This story draws attention to wisdom, knowledge, and the pursuit of truth. Proverbs 2:6 reminds us to meet sharp headlines with humble learning and wise application, asking how faithful people can respond with wisdom instead of noise.

title.en: Cuba receives China rice shipment amid US threats, blackouts
title.zh: 古巴在美国威胁和停电中收到中国大米援助

summary.en: Cuba has received a shipment of rice from China, which is expected to help alleviate food shortages. The island nation continues to face an economic crisis marked by blackouts and oil embargos, further complicated by threats from the United States.
summary.zh: 古巴已收到中国运来的一批大米，预计将缓解粮食短缺。该岛国持续面临经济危机，停电和石油禁运不断，而来自美国的威胁也使其处境更加复杂。

body.en:
Chinese aid is expected to alleviate food shortages in Cuba. But the island's economic crisis continues with blackouts and oil embargos are compunded by threats from the United States.

Cuba took delivery of 15,000 tons of rice donated by China on Sunday when the first of several promised shipments arrived at the port of Havana , helping to somewhat alleviate acute shortages on the Caribbean island.

"This noble gesture of solidarity will reach millions of consumers throughout all the provinces, in addition to our health and education institutions," Cuban President Miguel Diaz-Canel wrote on social media.

"The heartfelt ties of friendship and cooperation that unite [Cuba and China] are strengthened in crucial moments," he said.

Chinese ambassador Hua Xin said on Cuban television that the deliveries represent "the largest food aid" from China to Cuba "in recent years."

The shipment is the first batch of 60,000 tons of rice that Beijing has pledged to help combat a dire economic situation in the communist country which has only been exacerbated since the United States toppled Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro in January and halted exports of oil from Venezuela to Cuba.

On Sunday, up to 64% of Cuba was set to be subjected to simultaneous blackouts, according to data from the state-run Electric Union (UNE) compiled by the Spanish EFE news agency.

The Cuban government has recently acknowledged that the island's energy situation is "acute," "critical," and "extremely tense," with some blackouts in the capital Havana lasting 22 hours or more.

Last week, a record was set when 70% of Cuban territory was simultaneously without power during the moment of highest energy consumption. This week, the impact of these outages has fluctuated between 58% and 65% of the island.

The Havana government has called the current US oil embargo — which has been imposed on top of a general US trade embargo in place since 1962 — "genocidal" and has accused Washington of "suffocating" the island.

Cuba requires approximately 100,000 barrels of oil per day to meet its energy needs, only about 40,000 of which are supplied by domestic production. Various independent studies estimate that between $8 billion and $10 billion would be required to revitalize the Cuban energy system.

Meanwhile, US President Donald Trump 's administration continues to step up political pressure on Cuba , pushed by hardline Cuban-Americans in Florida, who have called for US-instigated regime change in their homeland for decades.

But ousting Diaz-Canel is unlikely to be as straightforward as the operation to remove Maduro in Venezuela in January, not least due to the lack of an obvious alternative.

title.en: China mine blast: Search and investigation continue
title.zh: 中国矿难：搜救与调查持续进行

summary.en: Chinese authorities have launched an investigation into "serious breaches" of security regulations following a coal mine explosion that killed at least 82 people. Two individuals remain missing after the incident.
summary.zh: 中国当局已对一起煤矿爆炸事故展开调查，该事故造成至少82人死亡，另有两人失踪，当局称事故原因系“严重违反”安全规定。

body.en:
Chinese authorities have launched an investigation into "serious breaches" of security regulations after an explosion in a coal mine left at least 82 people dead. Two people remain missing.

Authorities in China  on Sunday were still searching for two missing people and investigating a coal mine operator, after at least 82 people were killed in a gas explosion in a mine shaft on Friday.

A total of 247 miners were reportedly underground at the time of the blast at the Liushenyu coal mine in the northern inland province of Shanxi, with 128 subsequently taken to hospital.

While rescue teams continued to search for two missing people with the help of a robot which was sent into the shaft to test conditions, local officials accused the mine operator of "serious breaches" of security regulations.

A spokesman wouldn't specify what exactly the breaches were, but information reported by local media suggests several cases of operative negligence.

Some miners told the AFP news agency that they had had to purchase protective helmets with their own money while another report suggested that over half of the miners entered the mine shaft on Friday without having been properly registered with face recognition or issued with requisite tracking devices.

Officials have blamed "chaotic" scenes and "inaccurate" information provided by the mine operator for an initial death toll of 90, which had to be revised downwards, while state broadcaster CCTV reported that blueprints provided by the coal mine did not match the actual layout, hampering rescue efforts.

State media outlet Xinhua said one "responsible person" had been "placed under control" while the government in Beijing ordered a nationwide clampdown on "illegal and illicit activities," such as the falsification of security data, inaccurate tracking of miners' activities and illegal commissioning procedures.

Chinese President Xi Jinping called for a thorough investigation while a commentary in the official People's Daily newspaper on Sunday called for all regions and departments to learn from the accident and to "always keep safety in mind."

Shanxi Province is one of China's poorer regions and the center of the country's coal production. Despite the rapid expansion of renewable energies, China has the highest coal consumption in the world.

Mining safety in the country has improved over the past few decades; nevertheless, accidents continue to occur. In 2009, 108 people lost their lives in an explosion at a mine in the northeastern province of Heilongjiang.
body.zh: 煤矿爆炸造成至少 82 人死亡后，中国当局对“严重违反”安全规定的行为展开调查。目前仍有两人失踪。 周五矿井瓦斯爆炸造成至少 82 人死亡后，中国当局周日仍在寻找两名失踪人员并调查一名煤矿经营者。 据报道，山西省北部内陆省份六神峪煤矿发生爆炸时，共有 247 名矿工在井下，其中 128 人随后被送往医院。 虽然救援队在机器人的帮助下继续搜寻两名失踪人员，该机器人被送入矿井测试条件，但当地官员指责该矿经营者“严重违反”安全规定。 一位发言人没有具体说明违规行为具体是什么，但当地媒体报道的信息表明存在几起操作疏忽的案例。 一些矿工告诉法新社，他们不得不用自己的钱购买防护头盔，而另一份报告则显示，超过一半的矿工周五进入矿井时没有进行人脸识别正确登记或配备必要的跟踪设备。 官员们指责煤矿经营者提供的“混乱”场景和“不准确”信息导致最初死亡人数为 90 人，不得不向下修正，而官方电视台中央电视台报道称，煤矿提供的蓝图与实际布局不符，阻碍了救援工作。 官方媒体新华社称，一名“责任人”已被“控制”，同时北京政府下令在全国范围内打击“非法和不正当活动”，例如伪造安全数据、不准确跟踪矿工活动和非法调试程序。 中国国家主席习近平呼吁彻底调查，官方《人民日报》周日发表评论，呼吁各地区、各部门吸取事故教训，“时刻牢记安全”。 山西省是中国贫困地区之一，也是全国煤炭生产中心。尽管可再生能源迅速扩张，但中国的煤炭消费量仍居世界首位。 过去几十年来，该国的采矿安全有所改善；然而，事故仍在发生。 2009年，东北黑龙江省的一座矿井发生爆炸，造成108人丧生。

title.en: 'I shouted run': Witness recalls moment of China's worst mine disaster in years
title.zh: “我大喊快跑”：目击者回忆中国多年来最严重矿难发生瞬间

summary.en: A recent mining accident in China has been described as the country's deadliest since 2009, resulting in a significant loss of life. A witness recalled shouting for people to run during the incident.
summary.zh: 中国最近发生的一起矿难被描述为自2009年以来该国最致命的事故，造成了重大人员伤亡。一名目击者回忆在事故发生时曾大喊让人快跑。

body.en:
As emergency rescuers undertook a major rescue operation after Saturday's mining accident that killed at least 82 people in northern China, a wounded survivor said he heard no sound but smelled sulphur when the explosion happened.

"I didn't hear any sound at all, but then a cloud of smoke appeared," miner Wang Yong said.

"When I smelled it, it was the smell of sulphur like when people set off firecrackers. When the smoke came down, I shouted for people to run," he said.

"After more than an hour, I came to on my own, and then I woke up the person next to me" and got out, he told Chinese broadcaster CCTV.

The blast at the Liushenyu shaft in Shanxi province was the country's worst mining disaster in nearly two decades, with 247 workers underground at the time, according to Chinese media.

Hundreds of rescuers have rushed to the site, with medical teams taking 128 people to the hospital as of Saturday evening (local time), loaded into ambulances and carried on stretchers. Two people still remain missing.

Agence France-Presse journalists saw police blocking the road leading to the mine late Saturday, allowing only authorised vehicles to enter.

Helmeted rescuers took turns descending into the shaft overnight to look for the two missing workers, state media reported.

"As long as there is hope, we will make every possible effort," one rescuer told Xinhua news agency.

Chinese authorities launched an investigation into the blast, the worst since 2009 when 108 people were killed in a mine explosion in northeastern Heilongjiang province.

Preliminary findings showed the company operating the mine had committed "serious illegal violations", authorities told a press conference.

"Those found responsible will be severely punished in accordance with laws and regulations," they added.

A person "responsible for" the company involved had been "placed under control in accordance with the law", Xinhua reported.

The State Council, China's cabinet, ordered nationwide "tough crackdowns on illegal and unlawful activities", including the falsification of safety data, unclear headcounts of underground workers and illegal contracting.

Shanxi, one of China's poorer provinces, is the centre of the country's coal-mining industry.

Mine safety in China has improved in recent decades, but accidents still occur in an industry where safety protocols are often lax and regulations are vague.

In 2023, a collapse at an open-pit coal mine in the northern Inner Mongolia region killed 53 people.

China is the world's top consumer of coal and the largest greenhouse gas emitter, despite installing renewable energy capacity at record speed.

body.zh: 周六，中国北方发生了导致至少 82 人死亡的矿难，紧急救援人员在开展重大救援行动时，一名受伤的幸存者表示，爆炸发生时他没有听到任何声音，但闻到了硫磺的味道。 “我根本没有听到任何声音，但随后出现了一团烟雾。”矿工王勇说。 “当我闻到的时候，那是硫磺的味道，就像人们放鞭炮时一样。当烟雾降下时，我大声喊叫人们快跑，”他说。 他告诉中国中央电视台，“一个多小时后，我自己醒了过来，然后我叫醒了旁边的人”，然后下了车。 据中国媒体报道，山西省六神峪竖井爆炸是该国近二十年来最严重的矿难，当时井下有 247 名工人。 截至周六晚间（当地时间），数百名救援人员已赶赴现场，医疗队已将 128 人送往医院，并装上救护车并用担架抬上。目前仍有两人失踪。 法新社记者周六晚看到警察封锁了通往矿井的道路，只允许经过授权的车辆进入。 据官方媒体报道，戴着头盔的救援人员连夜轮流进入竖井寻找两名失踪的工人。 “只要有希望，我们就会尽一切努力，”一名救援人员告诉新华社。 中国当局对这起爆炸展开调查，这是自2009年黑龙江省东北部矿井爆炸造成108人死亡以来最严重的一次。 当局在新闻发布会上表示，初步调查结果显示，该矿运营公司存在“严重违法行为”。 他们补充说：“对相关责任人，将依法依规予以严厉处罚。” 据新华社报道，涉事公司一名“负责人”已被“依法控制”。 中国国务院下令在全国范围内“严厉打击违法违规行为”，包括伪造安全数据、井下工人人数不明和非法承包等。 山西是中国较贫困的省份之一，也是全国煤炭开采业的中心。 近几十年来，中国的矿山安全有所改善，但安全规程往往松懈、法规模糊的行业中事故仍然时有发生。 2023年，内蒙古北部地区一座露天煤矿发生塌方，造成53人死亡。 尽管中国以创纪录的速度安装可再生能源产能，但它仍然是世界上最大的煤炭消费国和最大的温室气体排放国。 在中国寂静的沁源县，煤矿工人有时会在张的烤串店吃饭，尤其是在发薪日，事故已经发生……

title.en: 'My dear friend': Putin and Xi praise partnership during talks in Beijing
title.zh: “我的挚友”：普京和习近平在北京会谈中赞扬伙伴关系

summary.en: Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping praised their partnership during talks in Beijing. China continues to be a significant and loyal economic partner to Russia, despite international economic and financial sanctions imposed on Russia by other countries.
summary.zh: 俄罗斯总统普京和中国国家主席习近平在北京会谈期间赞扬了两国伙伴关系。尽管其他国家对俄罗斯实施了经济和金融制裁，中国仍然是俄罗斯重要而忠诚的经济伙伴。

body.en:
Russian President Vladimir Putin has lauded his close ties with Chinese leader Xi Jinping, saying the nations are partners in trade and international affairs during bilateral talks in Beijing.

Xi welcomed Putin with a ceremony at the Great Hall of the People only days after meeting United States President Donald Trump.

The quick succession of Trump's and Putin's visits highlighted China's growing role as an international superpower, experts say.

Putin greeted Xi warmly as they met for the bilateral talks, describing the Chinese president as a "dear friend".

"We are truly delighted to see you. We keep in constant touch, both personally and through our aides in the government," he said.

Xi also stressed the "political mutual trust and strategic co-operation" between the countries, according to Chinese state media.

The two leaders have praised each other profusely in the past — Xi once describing Putin as his "best and most intimate friend".

Xi and Putin were set to focus on energy and security as well as their overall ties.

Chinese state media reported both parties agreed to extend a friendship treaty first signed in 2001.

China became Russia's top trading partner after Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.

China has said it is neutral in the conflict, maintaining trade ties with Russia despite economic and financial sanctions against Russia by the US and Europe.

China is the top customer for Russian oil and gas supplies, and Russia expects the war in Iran to increase the demand.

"The driving force behind economic co-operation is Russian-Chinese collaboration in the energy sector," Putin said.

"Amid the crisis in the Middle East, Russia continues to maintain its role as a reliable supplier of resources, while China remains a responsible consumer of these resources."

Xi stressed the need for the "complete cessation of hostilities" in the Middle East, according to Chinese state media.

"An early end to the conflict will help reduce disruptions to energy supply stability, the smooth flow of industrial and supply chains, and international trade order," Xi said.

A Russian presidential aide said earlier that Russia's oil exports to China grew by 35 per cent in the first quarter of 2026. Russia was also one of the biggest exporters of natural gas to China.

Putin said China and Russia's co-operation in foreign policy is "one of the key stabilising factors on the international stage".

In February 2022, just weeks before Russia invaded Ukraine, China and Russia announced a "no limits" partnership during a trip by Putin to Beijing.

Despite taking a neutral stance in the conflict, China supports Russia through frequent state visits, growing trade and joint military drills.

body.en:
Exclusive: BHP once dubbed climate change an ‘existential’ threat. But leaked documents show it has backtracked on decarbonisation at a vast network of mines

Temperature records tumbled. Frail, ill and elderly people died in their hundreds.

In a city not built for heat, trains were brought to a halt. Railway lines threatened to buckle and sagging power lines caused spot fires along the tracks.

Across the channel, Belgium, the Netherlands and Germany also hit record temperatures.

During the hottest week in late July, the then global chief executive of one of the world’s worst polluters was preparing to take the stage at a high-profile London event.

BHP’s Andrew Mackenzie stood before a collection of Britain’s most powerful – lords, MPs and diplomats – and gave a climate speech that made the world take notice.

Mackenzie warned that the world’s dependence on fossil fuels was causing risks that “could be existential”.

Global heating was indisputable, he said, and would have catastrophic consequences.

Here was one of the most powerful corporate leaders in the world making an impassioned call to arms on the problem his company helped cause. Mackenzie said global warming required the “biggest global mobilisation since World War II”.

The company later pledged to reduce emissions from its operations, largely from energy and diesel use at its mines, by 30% by 2030 and had already set a goal to reach net zero emissions by 2050. It also sought to curtail indirect emissions – from the use of its iron ore and coal by others – which at that stage were the equivalent of pollution from roughly 126m cars.

Six years after Mackenzie’s speech, long after he had left the company, senior BHP executives were presented with an internal memo dated May 2025.

The memo was about the company’s plans to decarbonise a significant contributor to its global emissions: the vast network of Pilbara mines, power plants, trains and diesel truck fleets that make up its Western Australian iron ore division.

The urgency for BHP to source renewables had “diminished”, it said. BHP was now claiming the plan it had devised to hit net zero in the Pilbara by 2050 had a “low probability of success”.

“To preserve optionality … alternate pathway decisions have been preserved and will continue to be assessed.”

The memo canvassed options that would massively delay key decarbonisation projects.

A huge wind and solar project, big enough to power roughly 150,000 homes, would be delayed, the memo said.

BHP then contemplated three “scenarios” that would put off the electrification of its highly polluting truck and rail fleets.

body.zh: 独家：必和必拓曾将气候变化称为“生存”威胁。但泄露的文件显示，该公司在大型矿山网络的脱碳问题上出现了倒退。 气温记录大幅下降。数百名体弱、患病和老人死亡。 在一个不适合炎热的城市里，火车停了下来。铁路线有弯曲的危险，电线下垂导致铁轨沿线发生局部火灾。 英吉利海峡对岸的比利时、荷兰和德国也创下了创纪录的气温。 在七月下旬最热的一周里，世界上污染最严重的公司之一的时任全球首席执行官正准备在一场备受瞩目的伦敦活动上登台。 必和必拓的安德鲁·麦肯齐 (Andrew Mackenzie) 站在英国最有权势的贵族、议员和外交官面前，发表了引起全世界关注的气候演讲。 麦肯齐警告说，世界对化石燃料的依赖正在造成“可能影响生存”的风险。 他说，全球变暖是无可争议的，并将带来灾难性后果。 这是世界上最有权势的企业领导人之一，他慷慨激昂地呼吁解决他的公司造成的问题。麦肯齐表示，全球变暖需要“二战以来最大规模的全球动员”。 该公司后来承诺，到 2030 年将其运营排放量（主要来自矿山的能源和柴油使用）减少 30%，并已设定到 2050 年实现净零排放的目标。该公司还寻求减少间接排放量（其他公司使用铁矿石和煤炭产生的排放量），该排放量在当时相当于约 1.26 亿辆汽车的污染。 麦肯齐发表演讲六年后，也就是他离开公司很久之后，必和必拓高级管理人员收到了一份日期为 2025 年 5 月的内部备忘录。 该备忘录涉及该公司计划对其全球排放的一个重要贡献者进行脱碳：构成其西澳大利亚铁矿石部门的庞大的皮尔巴拉矿山、发电厂、火车和柴油卡车车队网络。 必和必拓表示，采购可再生能源的紧迫性已经“减弱”。必和必拓现在声称，其制定的到 2050 年皮尔巴拉地区实现净零排放的计划“成功的可能性很低”。 “为了保留选择性……替代途径的决定已被保留并将继续评估。” 该备忘录探讨了将大幅推迟关键脱碳项目的选项。 备忘录称，一个足以为大约 15 万户家庭供电的大型风能和太阳能项目将被推迟。 必和必拓随后考虑了三种“情景”，以推迟其高污染卡车和铁路车队的电气化。 第一个选项被称为“中央”或“2035 财年部署”案例，将推动电池电动卡车和火车的推出最早可追溯到 2035 年——a...
